name: Church of the East

facts.value: organized under a catholicos at Seleucia-Ctesiphon by 280, independent of Antioch from 410

citations.locator: Holy Apostolic Catholic Assyrian Church of the East, member profile
citations.excerpt: In 280, the Church of the East was officially organized under the Catholicos-Patriarch Mar Papa bar Gaggai of Seleucia-Ctesiphon, and in 410 it renounced all subjection to the see of Antioch.
After Nestorianism was exterminated from the Roman empire, it found an asylum in the kingdom of Persia, whither several teachers of the theological school of Edessa fled.

facts.value: Repudiates the Council of Ephesus and the veneration of Mary as Mother of God, and traces its doctrines to Theodore of Mopsuestia.

citations.excerpt: The Nestorians differ from the orthodox Greek church in their repudiation of the council of Ephesus and of the worship of Mary as mother of God
The church traced its doctrines to Theodore of Mopsuestia rather than to Nestorius, whose name at first they repudiated, not regarding themselves as having been proselytized to any new teaching.

facts.value_before_verify: Does not accept the Council of Ephesus (431) or the title Mother of God for Mary, and follows the Antiochene theology of Theodore of Mopsuestia.

facts.value: The church in Persia, headed from 498 by a Patriarch of the East at Seleucia-Ctesiphon. Its missionaries reached China in the 7th century.

citations.excerpt: who in 498 assumed the title “Patriarch of the East” and had his seat at Seleucia-Ctesiphon on the Tigris

citations.locator: Assyrian Church of the East, member profile
citations.excerpt: In the 7th century they made their way into China.

facts.value_before_verify: The church of Persia and Mesopotamia, headed from 498 by a Patriarch of the East at Seleucia-Ctesiphon, whose missionaries reached Central Asia and China.

research_notes: Older sources call it Nestorian. The church itself rejects that label in part. Use neutral name.
